subject: Future Tech
title: Deuterium and Tritium
description: A quick, practical guide to Deuterium and Tritium.

hook.text: The easiest fusion reaction uses deuterium and tritium—two isotopes of hydrogen.

buildup.text: Deuterium is found in seawater. A bathtub of ocean water contains enough deuterium to equal 300 gallons of gasoline.

discovery.text: Tritium is radioactive with a 12-year half-life. It barely exists in nature. Reactors must breed it from lithium.

twist.text: The world's entire tritium supply is about 25 kg. A single fusion plant needs kg per year.

climax.text: Future reactors will surround plasma with lithium blankets that absorb neutrons and breed fresh tritium continuously.

punchline.text: Fuel from seawater. The hard part is the other half.
